acceptedWorkstreams.title: Add the invite emails each role receives, so admins can send them without writing anything
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The checklist tells admins what to do; the invites are where most setups stall. Approach: write ready-to-send invite messages for each role (department head, instructor, teaching assistant, student), each explaining in three sentences what Zedu is, why the department is using it and what to do first, with a placeholder for the workspace link. Check each step mentioned against the live app. Done: four invite templates, a one-page printable version of the checklist, and where each template fits in the checklist.

upvotes.reason: "Add the invite emails each role receives, so admins can send them without writing anything" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

Role-specific invitation copy explains the purpose and first action that a setup checklist alone cannot convey, while checking every named step against the live app avoids inventing onboarding capabilities.

This complements the approved department rollout checklist with copy-ready messages for the four people who receive an invitation. It can reduce setup friction without needing unsupported product claims, since the task calls for checking each step and keeps the workspace link as a placeholder.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Validate a single department setup, then expand the checklist to five
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Treat a university launch as a sequence of handoffs: the approved university admin, department lead, instructor and first learner. First verify each setup step in an approved test workspace, recording exact menu labels, required permissions and what success looks like. Then repeat the verified steps for five departments and mark where a decision or product limitation needs team confirmation. Deliver a reusable checklist with a one-department pilot path, the repeated steps for departments two through five, and clearly labelled blockers. This covers multi-department rollout and ownership, beyond the existing individual educator onboarding guides.

pendingIdeas.title: Add the un-onboard step: what a department does when its admin leaves mid-setup
pendingIdeas.description: Departments lose the person who started the setup more often than anyone plans for, and a checklist with no handover leaves five half-built departments. Deliver the handover page, the pending-invite check, and the one setting that decides whether the department survives the change.

pendingIdeas.title: Put dates on the checklist: what to do four weeks, one week and one day before term
pendingIdeas.description: A setup checklist used on the first day of term is used too late: invites go out after students have already organised elsewhere. Work: restructure the checklist by when each step must happen relative to term start, with the consequence of doing it late stated for each, and the two steps that can wait until week one. Deliver the timed checklist, the late-start variant for departments that begin mid-term, and the note on which step has a hard deadline because of the invite flow.

pendingIdeas.description: Most onboarding failures are discovered by a real lecturer who cannot see the channel they were told to use. pendingIdeas.title: Write the "keep this semester" list of tools the department should not migrate yet
pendingIdeas.description: Universities run timetables, grades and reading lists in systems Zedu does not replace, and a checklist that implies otherwise loses the admin's trust at step one. Work: name the three systems a department will keep, say what Zedu holds instead, and write the sentence that explains the boundary without sounding like a limitation. Deliver the boundary list, the wording, and the question an admin will ask next, with the answer prepared.

Naming the systems a department keeps stops the checklist reading as a rip-and-replace pitch, which is where administrators stop trusting it. The boundary sentence is what gets the rest read.

pendingIdeas.title: Write the one page an admin takes to IT: what is stored, who can read it, where files live
pendingIdeas.description: A department cannot finish onboarding without its IT or data officer approving the tool, and that approval does not come from a marketing page. Work: produce a single page with hosting and region, who can access department content, where uploaded files are stored, what happens when a member leaves, and what is exported at year end, each verified rather than assumed. Deliver the page, the source for each line, and the two answers that currently cannot be given, which are the ones IT will ask about first.
